output.brief:
The August drop was almost entirely a cooling failure. One chiller serving floors 6-8 broke on 4 August and wasn't repaired until 19 August. Rooms ran at 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and scores for stays checking out 5-20 August fell to 6.8. They recovered to 8.4 after the repair. Floors 1-5 stayed flat at 8.5, within normal variation. Of 74 negative comments, 56 were about heat, all from floors 6-8.

The evidence doesn't support blaming the housekeeping contractor or the kiosks. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and check-in scores are all unchanged, and kiosk queues are slightly shorter. I recommend you don't serve notice on Orrin or pull the kiosks. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value-for-money down a little on floors 1-5. That drop is only slightly bigger than the usual August dip, so I can't separate the two. Don't reverse the rate rise yet; keep watching it.

Next steps:
- Restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers.
- Stock critical spare parts.
- Write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages.
- Don't drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score. That would hide real information, and the score affects the leadership bonus.

I'm fairly confident (about 85-90%). I collected no further evidence.
